name: Epsilon Eridani b
tagline: Ægir — the nearest known Jupiter analog, swinging through the young star's dust belts.

facts.label: Type
facts.value: Gas giant — a colder, younger Jupiter echo

history: Ægir orbits the nearest Sun-like star — a restless, dust-ringed K2 dwarf only ~800 million years old. A gas giant of ~0.8 Jupiter masses on a notably eccentric 7.4-year loop, it sweeps in from ~4.6 AU to ~1.0 AU, ploughing through the system's inner debris belt twice each year. Its existence was debated for two decades — radial-velocity signals from an active young star are treacherous — but Hubble astrometry finally confirmed the giant's swing in 2019. Between the belts and the giant, Epsilon Eridani remains the nearest laboratory for how a young planetary system grows up.
